newsitem.title: USA: Occidental Q2 profits fall with oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Occidental Q2 profits fall with oil prices.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp reported lower second quarter profits on Thursday, reflecting falling prices for domestic natural gas and worldwide crude oil.
The Los Angeles-based oil company earned $158 million or $0.41 per share for the three months ended in June, down from $181 million or $0.49 per share in the comparable year-ago period.
Revenues were up $200 million to $2.7 billion from the second quarter of 1996.
Lower exploration costs and higher gas production partially offset weaker prices for hydrocarbons, the company said in a statement.

The company said its exploration and production division, responsible for finding and pumping gas and crude oil worldwide, earned $133 million in the second quarter, compared with $144 million a year earlier.

Earnings from the natural gas transmission division were $39 million, compared with $51 million for the second quarter of 1996. The decline in earnings resulted primarily from lower gas sales margins.
Chemicals earned $184 million, compared with profits of $160 million for the second quarter of 1996, before special items. The improvement in chemical earnings before special
items reflected higher profit margins in chloro-vinyls and petrochemicals and higher profits from specialty chemicals.
For the first six months of 1997, Occidental earned $337 million or $0.88 per share, compared with $315 million or $0.84 per share for the same period last year.
